title: Human Services payments on meal contracts per meal for older people
question: How much did the Human Services Agency pay on its meal contracts for each meal served to older people and adults with disabilities?
finding: Per meal (home-delivered and served at centres): $6.74 in 2019 and $9.44 in 2025 (+40%), as the money went from $19.4 million to $28.7 million (+48%) and the count from 2,873,470 to 3,039,789 (+6%).
how: Money: Human Services Agency payments to nonprofits on contracts whose title names home-delivered meals, congregate meals or nutrition services (emergency food, food-bank and pandemic food contracts are left out). Count: home-delivered meals plus meals served at centres, the aging department's yearly figures in the Controller's performance data.
limits: Contracts are picked by their titles, so a meal contract with an unhelpful title is missed and a nutrition contract that also pays for counselling is included. The City pays part of the cost of each meal; providers add federal, State and donated money. The meal counts come from provider invoices to the department, not from an outside count. Payments can land in a different fiscal year from the meals.
